questions.def: Use 'It' as a dummy subject when referring to weather.
questions.question: ___ is raining outside, so take an umbrella.

questions.def: Use 'There' to indicate existence or presence of something.
questions.question: ___ are many students in the classroom.

questions.def: 'It' takes the singular verb 'is' in this context.
questions.question: ___ a good idea to call her.

questions.def: 'It' is used as a dummy subject to introduce an opinion.
questions.question: ___ seems that he is not coming.

questions.def: 'There is' introduces the existence of something.
questions.question: ___ is a cat on the roof.

questions.def: Use 'It' to express importance: It is important.
questions.question: There is important to eat healthy food.

questions.def: 'It is' expresses a general statement.
questions.question: ___ difficult to learn a new language.

questions.def: 'It' is used to refer to time.
questions.question: ___ takes about an hour to get there.

questions.def: 'There are' introduces the existence of plural things.
questions.question: ___ are some apples in the fridge.

questions.def: 'It is' can refer to a future event.
questions.question: ___ my birthday next week.

questions.def: 'It' refers to the weather.
questions.question: ___ is cold today, wear a jacket.

questions.def: 'It' introduces an idea or suggestion.
questions.question: ___ seems like a good idea.

questions.def: 'It is' introduces a necessity.
questions.question: ___ necessary to finish the work today.

questions.def: 'It' introduces an important action.
questions.question: ___ is important to be on time.

questions.def: 'There are' indicates the existence of plural nouns.
questions.question: ___ are two chairs in the room.

questions.def: No error.
questions.question: It is raining very hard now.

questions.def: 'There is' introduces the existence of a singular noun.
questions.question: ___ a good restaurant near here.

questions.def: 'There' introduces a problem.
questions.question: ___ is a problem with my computer.

questions.def: 'It' introduces an easy task.
questions.question: ___ is easy to learn English.

questions.def: Use 'It' to introduce an opinion: It seems that...
questions.question: There seems that she is very happy.

questions.def: 'Traffic' is uncountable, so use 'is'.
questions.question: ___ a lot of traffic today.

questions.def: 'It' refers to the weather.
questions.question: ___ is sunny today.

questions.def: 'There are' introduces reasons.
questions.question: ___ are many reasons to learn a new language.

questions.def: 'It is' describes a situation.
questions.question: ___ a good time to go to the beach.

questions.def: 'It' introduces a likely event.
questions.question: ___ is likely to rain later.

questions.def: 'There are' means some cookies exist in the jar.
questions.question: ___ are some cookies in the jar.

questions.def: "It" is used as a dummy subject when the real subject is an infinitive.
questions.question: ___ is important to eat healthy food.

questions.def: "There" introduces the existence of something.
questions.question: ___ are many students in the classroom today.

questions.def: "It seems" is the correct form for impersonal expressions.
questions.question: ___ that he doesn't want to go.

questions.def: "There" introduces a fact or situation.
questions.question: ___ was a loud noise outside last night.
